translationRepairs: Early in the Tiancheng era his son Fa disinterred it and took it away.
Early in the Tiancheng era his son disinterred it and took it away.
其子發之攜去: 發之 is the verb phrase “disinterred/opened it,” not a personal name; inventing “Fa” as the son’s name is unsupported, and removing it restores the Chinese.
At the beginning of the Tiancheng reign his son Fa took it away.
At the beginning of the Tiancheng reign his son dug it up and took it away.
Literal English invents “Fa”; 發之 must be rendered as dug up/disinterred, and 攜去 as took it away—the proposed literal matches the Chinese.
Li declared himself acting commissioner and led soldiers and civilians in a memorial requesting formal appointment.
Yang Li declared himself acting commissioner and led soldiers and civilians in a memorial requesting formal appointment.
Subject 立 is Yang Li’s given name; bare “Li” in English reads as a Li-surname agent and conflicts with nearby 李繼珂. Expanding to Yang Li correctly identifies the referent.

Zhuangzong was furious and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack. Within a month the city fell. Li and more than ten of his accomplices were taken alive, sent to the capital, and dismembered in the marketplace.

Zhuangzong was furious and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack. Within a month the city fell. Yang Li and more than ten of his accomplices were taken alive, sent to the capital, and dismembered in the marketplace.
生擒立 is Yang Li (立), while 李紹真 is a different Li; bare “Li” after naming Li Shaozhen misattributes the captive. “Yang Li” disambiguates correctly.
Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Li had dared to hold it. Zhuangzong therefore ordered every circuit to dismantle its outer defensive works.
Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Yang Li had dared to hold it. Zhuangzong therefore ordered every circuit to dismantle its outer defensive works.
攻立輒敢據之 continues the Yang Li (立) rebellion narrative; English “Li” is ambiguous and should be Yang Li.
Before long Chongtao was killed on Siji's orders. The two men then turned on Dong Zhang. "Which door will you straddle now?" they demanded."
Before long Chongtao was killed on Siji's orders. The two men then turned on Dong Zhang. "Which door will you straddle now?" they demanded.
Chinese closes the dialogue at 何門？; the idiomatic already ends the quote at “now?”, so the extra closing quote after “demanded.” is a punctuation error with no source support.
